triggers: Large, novel, cross-cutting build: a full Next.js App Router learning project PLUS ~18-20 hands-on challenges spanning 12 topic areas (rendering, RSC, app-router, caching, server actions, route handlers/edge/middleware, data fetching, optimizations, SEO, deployment, TanStack Query, state management).
Educational project — no real user data, no real payments, no production auth/sessions. Auth and checkout are explicitly mocked / demo-scoped, which keeps this out of HIGH-risk production territory.

Security-EDUCATION dimension: challenges teach middleware auth, Server Action security (public POST endpoints), and Route Handlers. The reference solutions MUST model secure patterns, so a security review of the reference solutions is warranted even though there is no live attack surface.

Correctness-sensitive content: Next.js caching and RSC semantics are version-specific and have changed across releases (e.g. Next 15 changed fetch caching defaults, PPR is experimental). Teaching outdated facts is a real educational harm — version pinning and dated notes are required.
notes: Lane = feature-full because the scope is large / novel / cross-cutting (the default and fail-safe target), NOT because a production risk_flag is set. risk_level = MEDIUM (not HIGH) because there is no real PII / payment / production-auth surface; payments and auth are mocked/demo-scoped. feature-full already brings the full Phase-4 reviewer set including the security-auditor, which is the right level given the security-education content. sprint_count = 2 (MEDIUM + educational); a 3rd Red Team sprint auto-runs only if the internal plan score is < 8. Tags: frontend+backend+infra are all genuinely in scope; product tags the curriculum-scope decision (how many challenges) — applied by the orchestrator since .claude/project/business.md does not exist yet. No pricing tag (payments mocked).
